item.text: The current emphasis implementation is two conservative regular expressions, so it cannot represent delimiter runs, nesting, or the multiple-of-three rule. I’m replacing that narrow pass with a token-based delimiter stack that preserves already-protected code/links/HTML as opaque nodes and consumes delimiter runs one or two markers at a time.

item.text: The first scoped run exposed one state-handling bug: unmatched closing runs were being removed from the token stream instead of merely removed from the delimiter search stack, which dropped literal markers. I’m correcting that distinction; the matched spans themselves are already behaving correctly.

The emphasis section now passes all 132 owned examples. I’ve added focused regression tests for nested runs, unmatched delimiters, intraword underscores, and Unicode whitespace, and I’m running the project tests plus integrity checks on the read-only `sources/` assets.
